title: Hymns and funeral music in New Orleans and elsewhere
summary: Allen and Zander ask what was played at funerals; Love says only a few hymns like Nearer My God to Thee were known then.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: But they were playing the same things for funerals then that they play now?

No, it wasn't out of the money, you see. They didn't know nothing but the air, oh my God, that they in a few little hymns like that, you know. hymns out of any little book, play any kind of sacred music. It didn't have but that one thing that we buried in, the musicians, you see. They had a long piece of the paper by the time.
what was, what were some of the hymns they played here in the city though, about that time?

Oh, I can't think. A lot of them fellas got a lot of that music now, with Cornish had a whole lot of, close to Walt, or Dean, all those things. They didn't play that then, they didn't know it. Blue Red and all like that, they didn't know that. But it was hymns on that same order, you know. That was the only funeral they ever had a band with in the other example, when that boy died and we buried him.
But none of the other places had funerals, with music.
Yeah, yeah, they didn't have none in my home flat, none of the bad drugs, they didn't have none. Shreepo, oh yeah, that was the phone.
